prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System:Regional Flow Platform=Cedarbell;Meridian International Airport/Harbor East Airport/North Valley Airport/Lakeside Regional Airport/Southport Airport retain authority. Aliases:Airline Operations Coordinator=Saffron;Regional Flow Manager=Copperfin;Demand Prediction Service=Marlinstone;Weather Ingest Gateway=Orchard;Airport CDM Portal=Foxglove;Tower Supervisor=Brindle(drills);Ramp Control Lead=Quartzline(voice/chat);Slot Allocation Engine=Blueharbor(training);Slot Coordinator=Halcyon(voice conferences). Airline Operations Centre→Airline Interface Adapter→Flight Data Exchange:Flight Intent Message;Identity Access Service authenticates;invalid/incomplete rejected(reason-codes);material intents supersede schedules;changes require messages. Business Rules Registry governs carrier/fairness rules. Marlinstone+Capacity Assessment Module→Blueharbor:demand/intents/Airport Capacity Plan/Airport Acceptance Rate/runway-metering/sector-loading;capacity determines feasibility;Marlinstone flags Target Off Block Time imbalance. Blueharbor→Adapter/Foxglove:Calculated Takeoff Time/Target Off Block Time/arrival-opportunities;Calculated Takeoff Time combines runway-metering/departure-fix-loading/Ground Delay Program rules. Capacity precedes preferences;priority:safety/emergency/humanitarian/national-obligation>scheduled-commercial>discretionary;fairness mandatory. Copperfin authorizes Capacity Reduction State exceptions/recovery/divergence;Halcyon confirms publication,requests network-delay/fairness adjustments. Orchard validates weather/provenance/overrides;Storm Cell Snapshot confidence/degradation/provisional-capacity visible;Meteorology Briefing Officer interprets. East Apron Sensor/West Apron Sensor→Ramp Movement Board→Surface Surveillance Adapter→Foxglove:advisory movements;Board timestamps stand-readiness/boarding-completion/doors-closed/start-approval-readiness/taxi-start/configured-events. Quartzline reconciles,constraint-checks apron/stands/restrictions,sends Stand Tow Request Form;Blueharbor recalculates. Tower Supervisor/Airport Duty Manager resolve conflicts;Runway Inspection Note precedes capacity endorsement;North Runway Meter/South Runway Meter receive capacities;Alert Distribution Hub distributes approvals. Saffron checks readiness/crew/connections/recovery;shall confirm operator-requested revisions in Foxglove before freeze-horizon. Ground Handling Dispatcher milestone forecasts inform pre-freeze

New part:
S268: At the configured freeze horizon, the Regional Flow Platform locks the Target Off Block Time unless a rule-based exception or an authorized operational override is recorded.
S269: A frozen Calculated Takeoff Time may still be revised when the Slot Allocation Engine receives a capacity update that changes the feasible departure allocation for the affected traffic set.
S270: When a frozen value changes, the Airport CDM Portal requires a revised reason code and marks the earlier value as superseded rather than deleted.
S271: The Audit Event Ledger stores the previous value, new value, responsible user or automated function, timestamp, authority basis, and applicable operating state for every target time change.
S272: The Identity Access Service ensures that only users with the assigned operational role can approve frozen-time changes, manual exemptions, or retrospective corrections.
S273: The Data Governance Steward reviews audit samples to confirm that timestamps are complete, reason codes are valid, and manual changes can be traced to an operational justification.
S274: The Performance Analytics Warehouse uses frozen targets, actual milestone timestamps, and audit records to measure compliance, delay attribution, negotiation effectiveness, and rule quality after operations.
S275: The tower sequencing function translates the frozen operational targets from the regional flow process into an executable runway order for departures at Meridian Regional Airport.
S276: In this section, Tower Sequence Manager is also called Ironleaf for tower sequencing discussions.
S277: The Tower Supervisor is the operational owner of the departure sequence and uses the Tower Sequence Manager to confirm that each flight can be advanced without creating unsafe surface compression.
S278: The workflow starts when the Flight Data Exchange provides current flight intent data and the Departure Metering Service aligns each Target Off Block Time with the applicable Calculated Takeoff Time.
S279: The Tower Sequence Manager then builds a provisional order by runway, departure fix, aircraft wake category, and locally configured spacing rule.
S280: The North Runway Meter and South Runway Meter maintain separate queues, but the Tower Supervisor can view both queues together when runway balancing is required.
S281: The Surface Surveillance Adapter confirms whether an aircraft is still at stand, entering the movement area, holding short, or already committed to the departure stream.
S282: The East Apron Sensor and West Apron Sensor improve queue accuracy by detecting aircraft movement before manual ramp status updates are available.
S283: The Ramp Control Lead coordinates pushback release priorities against stand conflicts, taxi lane constraints, and the runway demand visible in the Tower Sequence Manager.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
